report.observed: The closed FCSTM model encodes two separate '[*] -> X' transitions (line 19 targeting HumanDrivingMode via Power_On, and line 21 targeting FinalState via Power_Off) but both are flagged as unreachable from a top-level initial entry (INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics at lines 19 and 21, and EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both Power_On and Power_Off events). verify_facts also show 'initial-entry:transition:line:19' and 'initial-entry:transition:line:21' as 'refuted', and the event-consumer checks for Power_On and Power_Off are refuted (reachable_consumer_transition_refs: []). report.reason: This is a structural issue because a UML initial pseudostate transition must be unconditional/untriggered, but the closed model attaches triggers (Power_On, Power_Off) to both root-level initial transitions, making them semantically unreachable (they can never fire since no trigger can be delivered to an entry that hasn't happened yet), which is confirmed by the deterministic diagnostics (INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL, EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE) and verify_facts refutations. report.claim: Top-level initial transitions for 'Power On' and 'Power Off' are unreachable, contradicting the required entry/exit behavior
report.where: transition: [*] (root initial pseudostate) -> HumanDrivingMode -> FinalState -> Power On -> Power Off
report.expected: Per NL3 ('when power on, the system turn into human driving mode') and NL5 ('when power off, it will transit to final state'), the machine should be able to actually execute these two initial transitions: on the Power On event the machine enters HumanDrivingMode, and on Power Off it enters FinalState. Both are modeled in the authored PlantUML as '[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On' and '[*] --> FinalState : Power Off', i.e. two alternative conditional entries from the same root initial pseudostate.
report.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts marks both entry transitions (transition:line:19, triggered by Power_On, and transition:line:21, triggered by Power_Off) as unreachable from a top-level initial entry (reachable_from_initial: false for both), and raises diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL for both lines plus EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both Power_On and Power_Off. verify_facts independently refutes 'initial-entry' and 'event-consumer' checks for both transitions. The root initial pseudostate '[*]' only has two outgoing edges, both of which are guarded by mutually exclusive triggers (Power_On, Power_Off) and neither is unconditional, so the closed model has no reachable unconditional path out of the root's initial pseudostate; both declared entries are therefore dead in the closed semantics even though the source clearly intends one of them to fire whenever the system starts. Author source: PlantUML line 2: `[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On`; PlantUML line 14: `[*] --> FinalState : Power Off`; PlantUML line 4: state `HumanDrivingMode` (explicit declaration); PlantUML line 14: state `FinalState` (implicit declaration).
report.reason: This is a genuine behavior-and-consequences defect: the closed model can never actually execute the state entry described by NL3 and NL5 because both root-level entries carry event guards that pyfcstm's initial-pseudostate semantics require to be unconditional, and no unconditional fallback exists (confirmed independently by reference_inspection_facts diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING at line 2, suggesting the very fix: add HumanDrivingMode as the unconditional initial target). Both the deterministic inspection facts and independent verify_facts concur, and the defect traces directly to the authored source lines (puml:2, puml:14) not to any compiler-owned wrapper element.

report.claim: Top-level initial transitions for 'Power On' and 'Power Off' are unreachable, contradicting the required entry/exit behavior
report.where: transition: [*] (root initial pseudostate) -> HumanDrivingMode -> FinalState -> Power On -> Power Off
report.expected: Per NL3 ('when power on, the system turn into human driving mode') and NL5 ('when power off, it will transit to final state'), the machine should be able to actually execute these two initial transitions: on the Power On event the machine enters HumanDrivingMode, and on Power Off it enters FinalState. Both are modeled in the authored PlantUML as '[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On' and '[*] --> FinalState : Power Off', i.e. two alternative conditional entries from the same root initial pseudostate.
report.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts marks both entry transitions (transition:line:19, triggered by Power_On, and transition:line:21, triggered by Power_Off) as unreachable from a top-level initial entry (reachable_from_initial: false for both), and raises diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL for both lines plus EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both Power_On and Power_Off. verify_facts independently refutes 'initial-entry' and 'event-consumer' checks for both transitions. The root initial pseudostate '[*]' only has two outgoing edges, both of which are guarded by mutually exclusive triggers (Power_On, Power_Off) and neither is unconditional, so the closed model has no reachable unconditional path out of the root's initial pseudostate; both declared entries are therefore dead in the closed semantics even though the source clearly intends one of them to fire whenever the system starts. Author source: PlantUML line 2: `[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On`; PlantUML line 14: `[*] --> FinalState : Power Off`; PlantUML line 4: state `HumanDrivingMode` (explicit declaration); PlantUML line 14: state `FinalState` (implicit declaration).
report.reason: This is a genuine behavior-and-consequences defect: the closed model can never actually execute the state entry described by NL3 and NL5 because both root-level entries carry event guards that pyfcstm's initial-pseudostate semantics require to be unconditional, and no unconditional fallback exists (confirmed independently by reference_inspection_facts diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING at line 2, suggesting the very fix: add HumanDrivingMode as the unconditional initial target). Both the deterministic inspection facts and independent verify_facts concur, and the defect traces directly to the authored source lines (puml:2, puml:14) not to any compiler-owned wrapper element.

report.claim: auto-final-triggered return transition is not independently guarded; it is folded into a single event alongside two unrelated event names
report.where: PlantUML line 13: 'AutonomousMode --> HumanDrivingMode : Human Steering Cmd, Brake Pressed, in (AutoFinal)'; FCSTM lines 13-15, 18: synthetic event Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal and guard R45RouteToken==5
report.reason: NL4.2 requires that AutonomousMode transition back to HumanDrivingMode under three distinct alternative conditions: receiving a human steering command, brake being pressed, or reaching the 'auto final' sub-state (i.e., 'in (auto final)' functions as a state-membership guard, not an event). The authored PlantUML instead writes a single transition labeled with one composite string as if it were one event: 'AutonomousMode --> HumanDrivingMode : Human Steering Cmd, Brake Pressed, in (AutoFinal)'. The FCSTM model preserves this by defining one synthetic event 'Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal' that fires from both AutoNavigating and AutoFinal sub-states, and a separate mechanism (a route token variable R45RouteToken set to 5 by that synthetic event, checked by guard 'R45RouteToken == 5' on the actual AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition) to route the return. This conflates three semantically distinct trigger conditions -- two external events (steering command, brake press) and one state-reachability condition (being in AutoFinal) -- into one indistinguishable trigger, and the 'in (auto final)' condition is never expressed as an independent guard on state membership; instead it is only reachable via the same merged event name being fired from within the AutoFinal state. This loses the semantic distinction required by the source text: the model cannot tell which of the three conditions caused the return transition, and 'in (auto final)' is not modeled as a guard evaluated on the AutonomousMode->HumanDrivingMode transition at all -- it is instead an artifact of which sub-state happens to also emit the same lumped pseudo-event. This is a genuine authoring defect (present already in the PlantUML label, not a translation artifact), since a competent state-machine author would model 'in (auto final)' as a distinct guarded alternative (e.g., using an automatic/completion transition out of AutoFinal, or a boolean guard checking current sub-state), and would keep the two external events as separately named triggers.

report.where: FCSTM lines 14-15: 'AutoNavigating -> [*] : /Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal effect { R45RouteToken = 5; };' and 'AutoFinal -> [*] : /Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal effect { R45RouteToken = 5; };'
report.reason: The requirement's phrase 'in (auto final)' (NL4.2) implies the return-to-human transition should be conditioned on the autonomous submachine actually having reached its auto-final sub-state, distinct from the other two return triggers (steering cmd, brake pressed) which are presumably valid at any point while in AutonomousMode. In the authored model (both PlantUML and FCSTM), the same merged trigger 'Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal' is attached both to AutoNavigating ('AutoNavigating -> [*] : ... effect { R45RouteToken = 5; }') and to AutoFinal ('AutoFinal -> [*] : ... effect { R45RouteToken = 5; }'), each independently setting the same route-token flag to 5. This means the 'auto final' portion of the condition has no distinguishing effect: whether the system is in AutoNavigating or AutoFinal, the same synthetic event with the same effect routes control back to HumanDrivingMode. Under one reading this is a direct consequence of the ambiguous single-label transition drawn by the author (see the related report on merged triggers), so it may be the same root defect rather than an independent one. Under an alternative reading, an author might have intended 'in (auto final)' purely as a documentation note that the steering/brake events can occur even while already in AutoFinal, in which case the flattened trigger is a legitimate simplification of a three-way OR condition and no separate defect exists beyond the merged-guard issue already reported. Given this competing plausible reading, this item is reported as D1 alongside (not replacing) the primary merged-trigger defect.

This means the 'auto final' portion of the condition has no distinguishing effect: whether the system is in AutoNavigating or AutoFinal, the same synthetic event with the same effect routes control back to HumanDrivingMode. Under one reading this is a direct consequence of the ambiguous single-label transition drawn by the author (see the related report on merged triggers), so it may be the same root defect rather than an independent one. Under an alternative reading, an author might have intended 'in (auto final)' purely as a documentation note that the steering/brake events can occur even while already in AutoFinal, in which case the flattened trigger is a legitimate simplification of a three-way OR condition and no separate defect exists beyond the merged-guard issue already reported. Given this competing plausible reading, this item is reported as D1 alongside (not replacing) the primary merged-trigger defect.

report.claim: FinalState is an unreachable dead-end / deadlock leaf with no outgoing transition, and its incoming transition originates from the root's initial pseudostate rather than from HumanDrivingMode
report.where: PlantUML line 2 '[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On' vs line 14 '[*] --> FinalState : Power Off'; FCSTM lines 19 and 21 (both '[*] -> ... : /Power_On' and '[*] -> FinalState : /Power_Off'); inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL (lines 19, 21), EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE (Power_On, Power_Off), LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING (FinalState line 17); reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF and W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING
report.reason: NL5 states 'when power off, it will transit to final state,' where 'it' refers to whichever operating mode (human driving or autonomous) is currently active -- i.e., the system should be able to transition to the final/terminating state from its live operating condition upon a power-off event, and NL-CONTRACT-NL5-ENDPOINT-1 explicitly expects a transition sourced from HumanDrivingMode (the continuing operating state) to Final. Instead, the PlantUML models power-off purely as a second, independent transition out of the *root* initial pseudostate: '[*] --> FinalState : Power Off' (line 14), parallel to and structurally identical to the power-on transition ('[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On', line 2). Both are modeled as initial-pseudostate transitions guarded/triggered by mutually exclusive events, rather than FinalState being reached via an outgoing transition from HumanDrivingMode (or AutonomousMode) while the system is actually running. The deterministic facts confirm this structurally: the inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics flag both 'INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL' (an initial pseudostate transition carries a trigger, at lines 19 and 21) and 'EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE' for both Power_On and Power_Off (their consuming transitions, lines 19 and 21, are never reachable from a top-level initial entry -- because only one of the two competing root-initial edges can ever actually fire). Additionally 'LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING' flags FinalState (line 17) as a reachable leaf with no outgoing transition, and reference_inspection_facts independently reports 'W_DEADLOCK_LEAF' for FinalState and 'W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING' for the root composite (noting the root has only conditional initial transitions, no unconditional fallback). The practical consequence is that the system as modeled cannot actually reach FinalState from a running HumanDrivingMode/AutonomousMode session at all -- power-off is only reachable as an alternative to the very first power-on choice at startup, not as a genuine shutdown from an active driving mode, which contradicts the natural-language intent that the running system 'transit[s] to final state' upon power off while it is 'it' (i.e., an already-entered operating mode).

report.claim: Power On and Power Off transitions are unreachable in the closed model
report.where: PlantUML lines 2 and 14; FCSTM lines 19 and 21; inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL (lines 19, 21) and EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE (Power_On, Power_Off); verify_facts non_proved checks initial-entry:transition:line:19, initial-entry:transition:line:21, event-consumer:Power_On, event-consumer:Power_Off
report.reason: The requirement (NL3, NL5) states 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode' and 'when power off, it will transit to final state', and the PlantUML encodes these as top-level initial transitions '[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On' and '[*] --> FinalState : Power Off'. In the FCSTM closed model these become '[*] -> HumanDrivingMode : /Power_On' (line 19) and '[*] -> FinalState : /Power_Off' (line 21). The deterministic facts explicitly flag both as problematic: inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics report INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL for both (an initial pseudostate transition carrying a trigger, which is unusual since initial transitions are normally unconditional/fireable exactly once at machine startup) and EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for both events, and verify_facts explicitly refutes 'initial-entry' and 'event-consumer' checks for transition:line:19 and transition:line:21 (reachable_consumer_transition_refs: [] for both Power_On and Power_On/Power_Off). In UML, an initial pseudostate's outgoing transition fires automatically at region entry and cannot be gated by an event trigger; by attaching the events Power On and Power Off to the root's initial transition, the model makes these transitions effectively unreachable/inconsistent with the semantics of an initial transition, meaning that after startup the machine can never actually respond to a 'Power On' or 'Power Off' event to reach HumanDrivingMode or FinalState via that arc — the only way HumanDrivingMode is ever entered is through the initial default-entry itself (which is not conditioned on an event) and FinalState is never reachable at all in practice, even though the requirement explicitly calls for a Power Off event to drive the system into the final state. report.claim: Missing unconditional root entry alongside two conditional entries (root initial pseudostate ambiguity)
report.where: Root state llms_emp_feedback_final_0000, transitions from '[*]' to HumanDrivingMode (Power_On) and to FinalState (Power_Off); PlantUML lines `[*] --> HumanDrivingMode : Power On` and `[*] --> FinalState : Power Off`
report.reason: The composite root state has two separate '[*] -> X' entry transitions guarded by distinct events: Power_On leading to HumanDrivingMode and Power_Off leading to FinalState. The diagnostic W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING notes there is no unconditional fallback entry. In classic UML semantics, the initial pseudostate of a region normally has exactly one unconditional outgoing transition that fires once when the region is entered; having entry only conditioned on distinct trigger events is atypical for an initial pseudostate, since initial transitions are usually completion-triggered, not external-event-triggered, and a region needs a deterministic single default entry. As authored, the root state's default/entry behavior depends on which of two mutually exclusive named events (Power_On vs Power_Off) arrives first, with no guaranteed default if neither occurs immediately; this could leave the machine effectively without an active state until one of these events fires. This is arguably how the author intended it (two initial-like transitions guarded by different power events, mirroring 'when power on ... human driving mode' and 'when power off ... final state' as two independent scenarios), which is a plausible alternative reading matching the informal requirements text. However, from a strict state-machine well-formedness perspective, an initial pseudostate ideally must have one unconditional transition, and modeling entry as two event-triggered transitions from '[*]' departs from that convention, and does not clearly guarantee reaching a state before any event fires. This is a defect only under the stricter reading of UML's initial-transition rule; under the looser 'entry event' reading commonly used in requirement translations, it is intentional and not a defect, hence D1.

report.reason: Transition_index 0 defines a transition from AutonomousMode to HumanDrivingMode guarded by `R45RouteToken == 5`, with effect `R45RouteToken = 0`. The variable R45RouteToken is written to 5 exactly when the Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal event fires from either AutoNavigating or AutoFinal (transition_index 6 and 7), but those same transitions immediately route to the outer '[*]' (i.e., to HumanDrivingMode via the root Power_On-independent path), not into the guarded transition at index 0. The var_dataflow block confirms R45RouteToken has empty top-level 'reads' and 'writes' lists at the variable-summary level despite the per-transition read/write records existing, suggesting the value-flow analysis found no consistent guard-satisfying path was traversed in the check, or that this transition (index 0) is dead code: it can only fire if R45RouteToken is already 5 while control is in AutonomousMode, but the assignments of value 5 occur on transitions that leave AutonomousMode/AutoFinal for '[*]' before this guard could be evaluated within the same micro-step, and no other transition sets R45RouteToken to 5 while remaining inside AutonomousMode. This looks like a translation-introduced construct not present in the original PlantUML (the PlantUML source has no analogous guarded variable-based transition at all — it only has plain event-triggered arrows). Since this transition and the R45RouteToken variable do not appear in the original requirements or PlantUML text, this could be entirely a translation artifact injected during FCSTM generation rather than an authored defect; alternatively, if the translator introduced this to encode the same 'Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed_in_AutoFinal doubles as brake-in-AutoFinal' semantics, it may represent an actual reachability defect where the encoded guard is never satisfiable, effectively creating a dead transition in the translated state machine. Given uncertainty about whether this variable/transition is an artifact of translation encoding (likely) versus an authored redundant/dead branch, this is flagged as ambiguous.

report.expected: Per NL1, after starting in PumpControl the system must be able to transition into its substates (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState). The authored PlantUML shows PumpControl's own [*] pointing to InitialState (line 5), which should presumably lead onward into the concurrent substate regions.
report.observed: In the authored PlantUML and in the closed FCSTM model, InitialState (PumpControl.InitialState) has no outgoing transition at all: the only transition touching it is the entry `[*] --> InitialState`. Deterministic facts confirm this: diagnostic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF flags 'InitialState' as a reachable leaf with no outgoing transition (reference_inspection_facts diagnostic at line 25; inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostic code LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at line 25), and verify_facts lists 'deadlock:state:InitialState:line:25' as refuted (i.e., the deadlock claim that it has an exit is refuted, confirming it truly has outgoing_count 0). Consequently PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState are all reported STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / reachable_from_initial:false, and the corresponding verify_facts reachability checks for PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState (and their children) are all status 'refuted'. report.claim: PumpControl's local initial pseudostate targets an unmodeled InitialState instead of PumpState
report.where: PlantUML lines 4-24 (state PumpControl block); specifically line 5 `[*] --> InitialState` and the concurrent region separators at lines 12/19; FCSTM diagnostics LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING (line 25) and STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL entries for PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState and their children.
report.reason: NL3 says: 'The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.' This requires PumpControl's local initial entry to lead into PumpState (directly or via a designated first substate). In the authored PlantUML, the initial edge inside PumpControl is `[*] --> InitialState` (line 5), and `InitialState` is a plain leaf state with no name tie to any real substate and, critically, no outgoing transition at all. PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState are instead only reachable via the concurrent-region separators ('--') without any entry edge from PumpControl's initial pseudostate. The three composite regions (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) each have their own *internal* initial edges to RunningState/MonitoringWaterFlow/MonitoringMethaneFlow, but per the FCSTM projection these regions are parallel orthogonal regions of PumpControl, not sequenced substates entered after InitialState. As a result: (1) PumpControl's initial entry never reaches PumpState as the narrative requires, and (2) InitialState is a dead-end leaf (confirmed by diagnostic W_DEADLOCK_LEAF / LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at line 25, and by reachability results showing PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState and all their children are unreachable from the top-level initial entry). This is a genuine author-modeling defect, not a translation artifact: the PlantUML source itself defines `[*] --> InitialState` and never wires InitialState onward, and separately declares the three states as concurrent orthogonal regions rather than a single sequential PumpState-first flow the requirement describes.

judge_field_audits.exact_text: NL3 says: 'The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.' This requires PumpControl's local initial entry to lead into PumpState (directly or via a designated first substate). In the authored PlantUML, the initial edge inside PumpControl is `[*] --> InitialState` (line 5), and `InitialState` is a plain leaf state with no name tie to any real substate and, critically, no outgoing transition at all. PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState are instead only reachable via the concurrent-region separators ('--') without any entry edge from PumpControl's initial pseudostate. The three composite regions (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) each have their own *internal* initial edges to RunningState/MonitoringWaterFlow/MonitoringMethaneFlow, but per the FCSTM projection these regions are parallel orthogonal regions of PumpControl, not sequenced substates entered after InitialState. As a result: (1) PumpControl's initial entry never reaches PumpState as the narrative requires, and (2) InitialState is a dead-end leaf (confirmed by diagnostic W_DEADLOCK_LEAF / LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at line 25, and by reachability results showing PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState and all their children are unreachable from the top-level initial entry). This is a genuine author-modeling defect, not a translation artifact: the PlantUML source itself defines `[*] --> InitialState` and never wires InitialState onward, and separately declares the three states as concurrent orthogonal regions rather than a single sequential PumpState-first flow the requirement describes.

report.claim: PumpState \u2192 WaterState and WaterState \u2192 MethaneState sequential transitions required by NL4/NL5 are missing; states are modeled as concurrent regions instead
report.where: PlantUML lines 4-24, particularly the '--' concurrency separators at lines 12 and 19 splitting PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState into orthogonal regions; FCSTM model text shows '[PlantUML concurrent region 0/1/2]' annotations and no cross-region transitions; NL segments NL4 and NL5.
report.reason: NL4 states 'The system can also transition to the WaterState substate' (implying a transition from the prior state, PumpState, to WaterState) and NL5 states 'the system can transition to the MethaneState substate' (implying a transition from WaterState to MethaneState). The obligation plan explicitly frames these as required transitions from PumpState to WaterState and from WaterState to MethaneState within PumpControl. The authored PlantUML instead places PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState as three separate orthogonal (concurrent) regions of PumpControl, separated by '--' (lines 12 and 19), with no transition connecting PumpState to WaterState or WaterState to MethaneState anywhere in the source. The FCSTM model confirms this: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState each have no outgoing transitions at the PumpControl level (outgoing_transition_refs empty for all three composite states), and reachability/verify_facts show WaterState and MethaneState are unreachable regardless. This is a genuine requirement-conformance gap: the natural-language description reads as a sequential progression (pump activation, then water monitoring, then methane monitoring) but the model instead expresses simultaneous independent regions with no linking transitions. An alternative reading is possible — the three could reasonably be independent concurrent monitoring functions of one composite state, which is a legitimate design choice for a pump controller — so this is not unambiguous. Given that the NL text uses transition language ('can also transition to WaterState', 'can transition to MethaneState') rather than 'concurrently monitors,' the sequential reading is well supported by the source text, making this a defect under one reasonable interpretation but not the only one.

report.claim: Composite substates PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState are never entered because PumpControl's initial transition only targets InitialState
report.where: PlantUML lines 4-25: `state PumpControl { [*] --> InitialState ... state PumpState {...} -- state WaterState {...} -- state MethaneState {...} }`; corroborated by fcstm diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL (lines 7-9,13-15,19-21) and LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING (line 25), and verify_facts reachability refutations.
report.reason: The author source (line 5) declares `[*] --> InitialState` as the only initial transition inside PumpControl. PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState (and everything inside them, including RunningState, MonitoringWaterFlow, MonitoringMethaneFlow, and their final-boundary states) are declared as concurrent orthogonal regions of PumpControl but there is no transition from InitialState (or any unconditional entry) into those regions. The deterministic facts confirm this: reachable_state_refs only lists llms_emp_feedback_final_0002, PumpControl, and InitialState; every state under PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState is flagged STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / W_UNREACHABLE_STATE, and verify_facts refutes reachability for PumpState, RunningState, FinalWaittr_0004, WaterState, MonitoringWaterFlow, FinalWaittr_0006, MethaneState, MonitoringMethaneFlow, FinalWaittr_0008. Additionally InitialState itself has no outgoing transition (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF), so the machine deadlocks in InitialState immediately after start. This directly conflicts with NL1/NL2/NL3, which state the system begins in PumpControl and 'can transition to different substates' including first transitioning to PumpState, then WaterState, then MethaneState. As authored, none of those substates is ever reachable, so the core behavioral obligation of the requirements (reaching PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState from the initial condition) is violated. An alternative reading is that InitialState was only meant as a transient placeholder and the author intended the orthogonal regions to run concurrently with InitialState rather than depending on it, in which case the real defect would just be a missing outgoing transition from InitialState (a dangling default entry) rather than a full unreachability of all three substates -- but even under that softer reading the regions PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState still are not entered by any transition originating from PumpControl's own entry, so the reachability problem persists under any reasonable reading, though the precise root cause (missing InitialState exit vs. missing region entry) is not fully certain, keeping this as D1 rather than D2.

report.claim: Initial pseudostate transitions in PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState regions carry event triggers, violating well-formedness of initial transitions
report.where: PlantUML lines 8, 15, 22 (`[*] --> RunningState : Activate Pump`, `[*] --> MonitoringWaterFlow : Start Monitoring`, `[*] --> MonitoringMethaneFlow : Start Monitoring`); corroborated by INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics on fcstm lines 10, 16, 22 and verify_facts initial-entry refutations.
report.reason: In UML, an initial-pseudostate outgoing transition is expected to fire automatically/unconditionally on entry to the containing region and should not carry a trigger or guard; it represents a completion transition, not an event-triggered one. Here, each orthogonal region's initial transition is written with an event label: `[*] --> RunningState : Activate Pump` (line 8), `[*] --> MonitoringWaterFlow : Start Monitoring` (line 15), and `[*] --> MonitoringMethaneFlow : Start Monitoring` (line 22). The deterministic facts confirm this is structurally present in the closed model: three INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL diagnostics fire (lines 10, 16, 22 in the FCSTM text) noting 'An initial pseudostate transition carries a trigger or guard,' and verify_facts explicitly refutes the initial-entry well-formedness check for all three (has_trigger: true, has_guard: false). This is a generic state-machine well-formedness concern independent of the specific requirement text: as modeled, entry into these regions requires an external event (Activate Pump / Start Monitoring) to fire before the initial default state is even entered, which is not how UML initial pseudostates are meant to behave, and it also means the pump/monitoring never starts on its own once the containing composite/region is entered. A competent alternative reading is that PlantUML permits labeling the initial arrow with a 'trigger' as an informal way of documenting the event that causes the pump/monitoring to begin, and some tools tolerate this notation loosely as an annotation on the state rather than a strict transition guard; under that reading the intent is just documentation and not a true guarded initial transition, which would make this a stylistic rather than a genuine violation. Given both the explicit tool diagnostics treating it as a genuine defect and the plausible documentary-intent reading, this is D1.

report.claim: PumpControl's initial state (InitialState) is a dead end that never leads to PumpState/WaterState/Methane regions
report.where: PlantUML lines 5-6 (`state PumpControl { [*] --> InitialState ... }`) and the orthogonal region separators (`--`) splitting PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState; translated model states 'llms_emp_feedback_final_0002.PumpControl.InitialState' and W_DEADLOCK_LEAF / W_UNREACHABLE_STATE diagnostics at lines 8-9, 14-15, 20-21, 25
report.reason: The requirements state that the system begins in PumpControl and from there transitions into the three substates PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState (reqs 1-5), with req 3 specifically saying the system 'first transitions to the PumpState substate.' In the PlantUML source, PumpControl is written as an orthogonal (concurrent) composite state using '--' separators, containing three parallel regions: an implicit region with only '[*] --> InitialState', and the PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState regions. Because InitialState is a plain leaf state with no outgoing transition, once the top region enters InitialState it can never leave, and this region has no relation at all to the PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState regions. The translated model confirms this structurally: 'InitialState' is a leaf with no outgoing transition (W_DEADLOCK_LEAF at line 25), and reachability_graph shows PumpControl only reaches InitialState, while PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState (and all their children) are flagged W_UNREACHABLE_STATE from the root entry path. This means the modeled top-level default path never actually enters any of the three substates the requirements describe, so the primary described behavior (entering PumpState, then WaterState/MethaneState monitoring) is not enterable via the state machine's initial/default flow. This is a genuine defect in the authored PlantUML (not a translation artifact): the author placed an orthogonal composite with a dangling 'InitialState' region alongside the three real functional regions, but never wired PumpControl's default entry to actually activate the PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState regions in a way reachable from '[*] --> PumpControl'. A competent alternative reading would be that PlantUML's default semantics for orthogonal regions is that all regions start concurrently when the composite is entered, so WaterState/MethaneState/PumpState regions would still be entered together with the InitialState region; under that reading the unreachability warnings are a translation/tooling limitation (the checker walking only one region) rather than an authors' defect. However, even under that concurrent-regions reading, the entry into PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState is guarded by events (Activate_Pump, Start_Monitoring) with no unconditional entry, so the sub-states themselves are never entered without an explicit event firing after initial entry -- but that is expected per requirement 1 ('transition based on specific conditions'). Given the affected leaf InitialState has literally no outgoing edge and no described relationship to pump/water/methane behavior in the requirements, this remains a modeling defect worth flagging, though the orthogonal-region alternative interpretation tempers full certainty, hence D1 would also be defensible; the strong tool corroboration (deadlock leaf, and three parallel regions totally unreachable per checker) supports raising it as a substantive finding.

report.claim: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState composite regions lack an unconditional default entry, contrary to entry obligation for composite states with only guarded initial transitions
report.where: PlantUML lines 8 ('[*] --> RunningState : Activate Pump'), 14 ('[*] --> MonitoringWaterFlow : Start Monitoring'), 20 ('[*] --> MonitoringMethaneFlow : Start Monitoring'); translated model diagnostics W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING for PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState
report.reason: Each of the three composite substates (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) defines its initial pseudostate transition only under a named event (e.g., '[*] --> RunningState : Activate Pump', '[*] --> MonitoringWaterFlow : Start Monitoring', '[*] --> MonitoringMethaneFlow : Start Monitoring') with no fallback unconditional '[*] -> X' transition. Per general UML state-machine well-formedness, an initial pseudostate transition normally should not carry a trigger/guard that could leave the composite state with no default entry target if the state is entered without that particular event context; here since these regions are entered as a whole only through orthogonal composite entry (not from an explicit external transition carrying the event), the guarded-only initial transition means these composite regions can never establish a current active substate on their own via default entry -- confirmed by the translated model's W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING diagnostics for PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState, each noting 'has no unconditional [*] entry transition.' This could be read as a genuine defect: the requirements state the system 'transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated' (req 3) and similarly for WaterState/MethaneState (reqs 4-5), implying these regions should have a well-defined default/initial active substate reachable without requiring an external event to simultaneously fire at the moment of composite entry. An alternative reading is that this is simply how PlantUML historically represents 'entry with trigger label on the initial arrow' as a stylistic/labeling shorthand for annotating what event is expected to cause entry into the region from the outside (i.e., activation is meant to be externally triggered, consistent with req 1's 'based on specific conditions'), in which case the guarded initial arrow is intentional and not a well-formedness violation. Given both readings are plausible and the requirements do not explicitly mandate an unconditional fallback, this is a D1-level concern.

report.claim: DoorsClosing's internal initial pseudostate targets itself, forming a self-loop that never reaches a real substate
report.where: PlantUML lines 4-6 ('state DoorsClosing { [*] --> DoorsClosing }'); corresponding FCSTM lines 8-10 with synthesized state InvalidInitialtr_0002
report.reason: The PlantUML source authors 'state DoorsClosing { [*] --> DoorsClosing }' (line 5), i.e. an initial pseudostate inside the DoorsClosing composite that points back at DoorsClosing itself rather than at a distinct internal substate. Since DoorsClosing has no other internal children, this inner initial edge is a self-referencing/circular construct with no real semantic content, and the FCSTM translator had to synthesize a placeholder substate 'InvalidInitialtr_0002' (named literally 'PlantUML initial target outside child scope: DoorsClosing') to make the initial-pseudostate rule resolvable at all. The deterministic facts confirm this: reference_inspection_facts flags W_DEADLOCK_LEAF on the synthesized leaf, and inspection_equivalent_facts shows 'InvalidInitialtr_0002' as a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions, exactly the sort of construct the translator manufactures when the authored model does not have a legal well-formed initial-pseudostate target. This is an authored well-formedness defect: an initial pseudostate must target a proper distinct vertex within the composite's region, not the composite state itself, and here the composite has no other substates to target, so the construct is meaningless/malformed as authored, independent of any translation artifact.

report.reason: The PlantUML source at line 4-6 declares `state DoorsClosing { [*] --> DoorsClosing }`. This creates a nested initial pseudostate inside DoorsClosing whose target is DoorsClosing itself. Since DoorsClosing is a composite state (per exact_source_inventory, kind: composite, line 4) with a nested initial transition pointing back to its own container name, the initial arrow does not resolve to any distinct child substate. report.claim: EmergencyStopping is a terminal deadlock state with no outgoing transition
report.where: PlantUML lines 32-36 (state EmergencyStopping block, no outgoing transition anywhere in source); FCSTM diagnostic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at state:EmergencyStopping:line:31; reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF for llms_emp_feedback_final_0004.EmergencyStopping
report.reason: The requirement (NL3) states: 'When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.' Nothing in the natural language ever describes what happens after EmergencyStopping is entered - there is no described exit or recovery path. In the authored PlantUML, EmergencyStopping is declared (lines 32-35) with entry/do actions but no outgoing transition anywhere in the diagram. The FCSTM model and both deterministic backends confirm this: inspection_equivalent_facts lists diagnostic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING for 'EmergencyStopping' (line 31) with the message 'Reachable leaf state ... has no outgoing FCSTM transition', and reference_inspection_facts likewise reports W_DEADLOCK_LEAF for llms_emp_feedback_final_0004.EmergencyStopping with reason 'no_outgoing_transition' and a suggested fix to add an exit transition. Verify_facts also lists the deadlock check for EmergencyStopping as 'refuted' (i.e., a deadlock exists) rather than proved absent. For a state machine intended to model an operational system (a train control system, per context), reaching a state with literally no way to leave is a structural dead end; many practitioners would treat a designed final resting point (e.g., an explicit final state, or a manual-reset transition back to an operational state) as an implicit obligation even when the prose doesn't spell out the recovery path, since the model is otherwise a live, cyclable operational description. This constitutes a defect: the modeled behavior forecloses any further defined behavior after an emergency stop, which is a strong candidate for an unstated implicit completeness obligation. A competent alternative reading: the requirements may simply intend EmergencyStopping (like Stopping) to be a true terminal end-state of the scenario being modeled (the journey/scenario ends when an emergency stop occurs, requiring external/manual intervention not in scope of this diagram), in which case having no outgoing transition is intentional and matches the source text, which never mentions leaving EmergencyStopping. Given this legitimate alternative, this is D1, not D2.

report.claim: DoorsClosing has a self-loop initial transition instead of progressing to a real substate
report.where: PlantUML block: 'state DoorsClosing { [*] --> DoorsClosing }'; reflected in translated model as state llms_emp_feedback_final_0004.DoorsClosing.InvalidInitialtr_0002 with initial_targets pointing to it.
report.reason: The PlantUML source contains: `state DoorsClosing { [*] --> DoorsClosing }`. This is a malformed/degenerate nested-initial transition: the initial pseudostate inside the composite state DoorsClosing points back to the same composite state DoorsClosing (its own container) rather than to a genuine leaf substate. In the translated FCSTM, this shows up as the synthetic substate 'llms_emp_feedback_final_0004.DoorsClosing.InvalidInitialtr_0002', which the inspection flags as the initial target of DoorsClosing, and diagnostics show it has no outgoing transition of its own within the composite besides the forced Closed_SendDeparted transition escaping to [*]. This is a genuine authoring defect in the PlantUML, not an artifact of translation: the source literally writes an initial arrow to the containing state's own name, which is not a valid nested state and produces a structurally meaningless self-referential region. A composite state's initial pseudostate must target a distinct child state; here it does not, so DoorsClosing's internal region has no real, reachable substate structure, violating basic state machine well-formedness (an initial transition must lead to a legitimate vertex within the region, not recreate the parent name as a pseudo-child).

report.claim: EmergencyStopping is a deadlock leaf state with no way to finish or exit
report.where: PlantUML: 'state EmergencyStopping { ... }' block with no outgoing transition; translated model: state llms_emp_feedback_final_0004.EmergencyStopping, diagnostic W_DEADLOCK_LEAF at span lines 31-34.
report.reason: Requirement 3 says: 'When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions Emergency Stop and sends the Obstacle Detected signal.' Neither the requirements nor the PlantUML specify any transition leaving EmergencyStopping (source: `state EmergencyStopping { EmergencyStopping: entry/Emergency Stop \n EmergencyStopping: do/Send Obstacle Detected }` with no outgoing arrow). The inspection confirms this structurally: diagnostic W_DEADLOCK_LEAF states 'Leaf state llms_emp_feedback_final_0004.EmergencyStopping has no outgoing transition' and the reachability_graph confirms EmergencyStopping maps to an empty list of reachable states. This is a genuine modeling gap: a state reached via a stop-the-world safety event with no completion transition leaves the composite region (and thus the whole machine, since EmergencyStopping is a direct child of the root) permanently stuck once an obstacle is detected, with no way to model recovery, operator reset, or session completion. An alternative reading is that EmergencyStopping is deliberately designed as a true terminal/absorbing state representing an unrecoverable safety condition that requires external system restart outside the scope of this diagram, which is a common and defensible design choice for emergency-stop semantics; this is why I do not treat it as a certain defect. But because the requirements describe an ongoing system with normal signal-processing behavior elsewhere and give no explicit indication that emergency stop is meant to be irrecoverable forever, the deadlock leaf remains a plausible unaddressed obligation for finishing/exiting a leaf into its parent, especially since sibling states like Stopping share the same unresolved treatment.

report.claim: DoorOpenWithItem alternatives from NL4 are not mutually exclusive / underspecified guard relationship
report.where: PlantUML lines 13-15 (DoorIdleWithItem transitions); exact_source_inventory tr_0007 'Close Door with Zero Time', tr_0008 'Enter Cooking Time'
report.reason: NL4 states two alternatives from DoorOpenWithItem: closing the door with zero time set (-> DoorShutWithItem) or entering cooking time (-> ReadytoCook). In the PlantUML/FCSTM model, these are modeled as two different events (Close Door with Zero Time vs Enter Cooking Time) on the DoorIdleWithItem sub-state, which are inherently distinguishable event triggers, so guard disjointness holds via event separation. However, the natural language phrasing ('if the door is closed with zero time set') suggests a guarded transition on a 'door closed' event conditioned by a time value, rather than a wholly distinct event. The model instead invents a bespoke event 'Close Door with Zero Time' distinct from the plain 'Close Door' used elsewhere (DoorOpen -> DoorShut), meaning there is no general 'door closed with nonzero time' transition captured from DoorIdleWithItem at all -- if the door is closed with nonzero (or unset) time from DoorIdleWithItem, no transition is defined, silently blocking that event. This could be read either as an acceptable modeling choice (splitting the guarded transition into a separately named event) or as an incompleteness defect, since the NL implies 'door closed' is the action and 'zero time set' is a condition on it, and the reverse condition (non-zero time) has no defined outgoing behavior from DoorIdleWithItem, leaving door-close-with-nonzero-time unhandled while the sibling top-level state DoorOpen/DoorShut only knows plain 'Close Door'.

report.claim: DoorShut has a dangling 'Cancel' body action with no defined effect or transition
report.where: PlantUML source line 3-4: 'DoorShut : Cancel'; canonical IR state DoorShut source_id 'DoorShut' line 2; FCSTM state DoorShut named "DoorShut\n[PlantUML body] Cancel"; NL requirement segment NL1.
report.reason: The requirement (NL1) states: 'From this state [DoorShut], the system can either remain in DoorShut if a Cancel action is performed or transition to the DoorOpen state when the door is opened.' The PlantUML author-source encodes this as an internal state annotation: 'DoorShut : Cancel' (line 3-4 in llms_emp_feedback_final_0005.puml, source_id state:DoorShut, line 2 in canonical IR). However, this is only a text label/state-body note attached to DoorShut, not an actual self-transition or internal transition triggered by a Cancel event. In the FCSTM closed model, DoorShut is rendered as 'state DoorShut named "DoorShut\n[PlantUML body] Cancel"' with only one outgoing transition (DoorShut -> DoorOpen on Door_Opened, transition:line:57). There is no modeled response to a Cancel event while in DoorShut: no self-loop transition, no guard, no effect. The requirement explicitly describes Cancel as an action that keeps the system in DoorShut, implying it should be an explicit (even if no-op) response to that event in that state. As authored, PlantUML syntax for 'DoorShut : Cancel' is ambiguous — it could be read purely as a documentation/note listing an activity or action name within the state (a common PlantUML idiom for internal doings), rather than as a request for a modeled self-transition. This makes it a defect under the interpretation that the author intended a real Cancel-triggered self-loop (unrepresented behavior, an omitted transition), but a competent alternative reading treats this as an annotation only, with no obligation to formalize it as a transition, since PlantUML's textual body syntax is inherently for notes/activities, not transitions. Given this genuine ambiguity between 'missing self-transition semantics' and 'note-only annotation', a D1 rating (violation reading survives but a competent alternative exists) is appropriate.

Since the root-level initial transition goes to InitialState (line 2: '[*] --> InitialState'), and InitialState only transitions out via 'Collision Resolved' back-edge target, there should be some path from InitialState (or root) into CollisionDetection so the detection process, and hence eventual sub-machine activation, can actually occur.
report.observed: In the closed FCSTM model and deterministic facts, CollisionDetection has no incoming transition from InitialState or from the root '[*]'; the only root-level initial transition is '[*] -> InitialState' (tr_0001), and InitialState has no outgoing transitions in the authored PlantUML (confirmed by reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostic for InitialState, line 59, 'Reachable leaf state InitialState has no outgoing FCSTM transition'). CollisionDetection, PossibleCollision, and CollisionAvoidance are all flagged STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / reachability refuted in inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts. This means the sub-machine described by NL2 can never actually become active in the closed model because the entire CollisionDetection->CollisionAvoidance->InitialState cycle is disconnected from the reachable root, contradicting the requirement that detecting a collision triggers activation. report.expected: Per NL2, the CollisionAvoidance sub-machine 'becomes active' when a collision is detected, and per NL3 its orthogonal regions should then allow concurrent activation of the different collision-avoidance controls (braking, steering, alerts). The only reachable states are the root and InitialState. Consequently the collision-avoidance sub-machine described in NL2/NL3 can never become active in the closed model, so the concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls that NL3 asserts can never actually occur. report.expected: Per NL2, the CollisionAvoidance sub-machine ('This sub-machine') should become active (reachable/entered) precisely when a collision of one of the three types is detected inside CollisionDetection, via the 'Collision Mode Active' transition from CollisionDetection to CollisionAvoidance. Since the root-level initial transition goes to InitialState (line 2: '[*] --> InitialState'), and InitialState only transitions out via 'Collision Resolved' back-edge target, there should be some path from InitialState (or root) into CollisionDetection so the detection process, and hence eventual sub-machine activation, can actually occur.
report.observed: In the closed FCSTM model and deterministic facts, CollisionDetection has no incoming transition from InitialState or from the root '[*]'; the only root-level initial transition is '[*] -> InitialState' (tr_0001), and InitialState has no outgoing transitions in the authored PlantUML (confirmed by reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostic for InitialState, line 59, 'Reachable leaf state InitialState has no outgoing FCSTM transition'). CollisionDetection, PossibleCollision, and CollisionAvoidance are all flagged STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL / reachability refuted in inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts. This means the sub-machine described by NL2 can never actually become active in the closed model because the entire CollisionDetection->CollisionAvoidance->InitialState cycle is disconnected from the reachable root, contradicting the requirement that detecting a collision triggers activation. report.claim: CollisionAvoidance is never entered because the top-level model has no transition into it triggered by the three collision-detection events
report.where: PlantUML lines 31-32 (CollisionDetection -down-> CollisionAvoidance : Collision Mode Active); FCSTM lines 26-29 (Collision_Mode_Active transitions); NL2
report.reason: NL2 says: "This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected." The PlantUML models this with a plain, unlabeled arrow at the top level: `CollisionDetection -down-> CollisionAvoidance : Collision Mode Active`. The inner CollisionDetection sub-machine reacts to 'Frontend Detected', 'Rear-end Detected', and 'Pedestrian Detected' by moving from PossibleCollision into FrontendCollision/RearendCollision/PedestrianCollision, but none of those inner leaf states has any outgoing transition back out to trigger the outer 'Collision Mode Active' edge. In the PlantUML there is simply no path from FrontendCollision/RearendCollision/PedestrianCollision to the boundary that fires 'Collision Mode Active', so activation of CollisionAvoidance is structurally disconnected from the three named detection events, even though NL2 requires exactly that causal link. In the FCSTM working representation this is reflected as literal exit transitions from PossibleCollision, FrontendCollision, RearendCollision, and PedestrianCollision to `[*]` emitting Collision_Mode_Active with `R45RouteToken = 15`, but these are compiler-synthesized completion transitions for the composite-to-composite boundary crossing, not source-authored transitions guarded by the three detection events themselves; the deterministic facts also flag 'Collision_Mode_Active' as an event whose consumers are unreachable from the top-level initial entry. A competent alternative reading is that PlantUML's composite-to-composite arrow syntax is understood by the tool to mean 'exit the composite state (from whichever substate is active) via this single labeled edge,' so the diagram may be intended to convey that any of the three detected-collision substates causes the outer transition — this is a common, accepted PlantUML idiom, and the label 'Collision Mode Active' could be read as the umbrella event fired once any of the three specific detections has occurred. Under that reading the model is not defective, only implicit. Because both readings are plausible, this is a D1 not a D2.

report.claim: Top-level state machine has no reachable path to CollisionAvoidance, CollisionDetection, or OperationalControls from the true initial state
report.where: PlantUML lines 2, 30-32 (top-level [*] --> InitialState; CollisionDetection -down-> CollisionAvoidance; CollisionAvoidance --> InitialState); FCSTM lines 59-62; inspection_equivalent_facts reachability and LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostics
report.reason: The overall diagram's initial pseudostate goes `[*] --> InitialState`, and the only other top-level transitions are `InitialState` having no outgoing edge at all, while `CollisionDetection`, `CollisionAvoidance`, and `OperationalControls` are connected to each other and to InitialState only via `Collision Mode Active` and `Collision Resolved`, none of which originates from InitialState. The deterministic facts confirm this directly: reachable_state_refs is only `["state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0007", "state:InitialState"]`, with CollisionDetection, CollisionAvoidance, and OperationalControls all marked reachable_from_initial: false, and InitialState itself is flagged LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING ('Reachable leaf state InitialState has no outgoing FCSTM transition'). This means, as authored, the machine can never leave InitialState and enter the collision-detection/avoidance machinery at all — a basic well-formedness/progress obligation (every non-terminal state should be able to make progress, and states meant to be operative should be reachable) is violated. A plausible alternative reading is that PlantUML's implicit fall-through semantics intend InitialState to be a transient placeholder whose real behavior is 'go do collision detection continuously,' and the diagram author simply forgot to draw an outgoing edge from InitialState to CollisionDetection, treating this as an authoring omission rather than a deliberate deadlock. Since the natural-language text (NL2, NL3) describes the collision sub-machine as being 'active' in a meaningful operational sense, and OperationalControls's states also being permanently unreachable seems inconsistent with the requirements' intent that operational controls should run, this looks like a genuine gap, but because it could also be read as an intentionally minimal 'placeholder' skeleton diagram, I record it as D1.

report.claim: No transition connects InitialState to CollisionDetection, so the collision-detection sub-machine is unreachable
report.where: PlantUML lines 2, 4-9, 31-33; top-level transitions block (no InitialState->CollisionDetection edge); FCSTM lines 22/60/62; inspection_equivalent_facts STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for CollisionDetection and children; verify_facts reachability checks refuted for state:CollisionDetection:line:17 etc.
report.reason: The natural-language requirement (NL2) says the collision-detection sub-machine 'becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected,' implying it is entered from the machine's normal running state and can actually detect these events. In the authored PlantUML, the top-level flow is only `[*] --> InitialState`, `CollisionDetection -down-> CollisionAvoidance : Collision Mode Active`, and `CollisionAvoidance --> InitialState : Collision Resolved`. report.claim: InitialState is a terminal leaf with no outgoing transition after the machine returns to it from CollisionAvoidance
report.where: PlantUML line 2 (`[*] --> InitialState`) and absence of any transition from InitialState; FCSTM line 59 (`state InitialState named \"InitialState\";` with no outgoing edge); inspection_equivalent_facts LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING at line 59; reference_inspection_facts W_DEADLOCK_LEAF for InitialState; verify_facts deadlock check for state:InitialState:line:59 refuted.
report.reason: The requirements describe a cyclical safety flow: detection triggers avoidance ('Collision Mode Active'), avoidance completion returns control ('Collision Resolved' -> InitialState). This implies InitialState should be able to restart the detection cycle (re-enter CollisionDetection) once returned to. In the authored PlantUML/FCSTM, InitialState has no outgoing transition at all (`state InitialState named \"InitialState\";` with no exit edge), so after `CollisionAvoidance --> InitialState : Collision Resolved` fires, the machine is permanently stuck in InitialState with no way to re-detect a collision or reach any other region. This is flagged as LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF for InitialState in both the inspection_equivalent_facts and reference_inspection_facts, and the deadlock check for state:InitialState:line:59 is 'refuted' (outgoing_count: 0) in verify_facts. A competent alternative reading is that InitialState is legitimately intended as a final quiescent state (the model's only transition into it is a 'Collision Resolved' terminal state, and the requirement text does not explicitly demand a repeating cycle), so this could be an intentional single-shot design. Given that ambiguity, but also given the naming ('InitialState' suggesting a restart point after which the same PlantUML shows no path back into CollisionDetection anyway, compounding issue 1) this is best treated as a real but debatable defect.

report.claim: CollisionAvoidanceSystem region is never reachable from the machine root
report.where: PlantUML lines 51-59 (CollisionAvoidanceSystem declaration and transitions); FCSTM state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:73 and children; inspection_equivalent_facts diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL and EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE
report.reason: The requirements describe the collision avoidance system as a concurrently-active safety function that must be able to activate/deactivate at any time based on driving conditions (pedestrian detection, rear/front distances, mode-dependent thresholds referencing high_way/urban_way). In the authored PlantUML, CollisionAvoidanceSystem is declared as a sibling top-level state to AutonomousMode, but the only root-level initial transition is '[*] --> AutonomousMode'; there is no initial edge, orthogonal-region separator, or any transition from AutonomousMode/root into CollisionAvoidanceSystem. As a result CollisionAvoidanceSystem and both of its substates (collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active) are structurally unreachable from the machine's initial state. This is confirmed by the deterministic facts: inspection_equivalent_facts marks 'CollisionAvoidanceSystem', 'collision_avoidance_deactive', and 'collision_avoidance_active' as reachable_from_initial: false, verify_facts refutes reachability for all three, and reference_inspection_facts raises W_UNREACHABLE_STATE warnings for the deactive/active states. Both activation-condition and deactivation-condition transitions (event consumers) are also flagged EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE. Since the NL explicitly requires this subsystem to operate as an active safety monitor throughout driving (NL12/NL13), never entering it is a genuine defect, not merely a translation artifact -- the PlantUML source itself (author_source, lines 51-59) lacks any connecting transition. An alternative reading is that the author intended two independent, always-running orthogonal regions (a common state-machine idiom for a monitor running in parallel with the main mode machine) and PlantUML's flat top-level state list is just an imperfect textual encoding of that intent; under that reading the composite is meant to be concurrently active by convention rather than entered via a transition. However, plain top-level states in PlantUML (not enclosed in an explicit '--' orthogonal region syntax) are not concurrent regions by default, and the model as authored provides no other entry path, so the more directly supported reading is that the region is simply disconnected/unreachable.

report.claim: Guards for InitialState->HighwayMode/UrbanMode split, and enter_hwy/cruise dual outgoing guards, are not mutually exclusive, creating nondeterminism
report.where: PlantUML lines 8-10 (InitialState guards) and lines 16-17 (enter_hwy guards); contracts NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DISJOINT-1 and NL-CONTRACT-NL12-DISJOINT-1; transition group NL-GROUP-NL3-1
report.reason: The requirement (NL2) frames high_way=true and urban_way=true as alternative, presumably mutually exclusive conditions selecting one mode from InitialState. Similarly, NL3 describes enter_hwy transitioning to cruise when the front distance is NOT close and to lane_change when it IS close and an extra lane is available -- implying complementary, non-overlapping guards. However neither the NL text nor the model establishes disjointness: both high_way=true and urban_way=true could in principle be simultaneously true (nothing states they are complementary boolean flags), and per the working PlantUML/FCSTM, enter_hwy's two outgoing transitions use event names 'dist_to_front>=25' (tr_0006) and 'dist_to front<25 && extra_lane=true' (tr_0007) which are complementary only when extra_lane=true; if extra_lane=false and dist_to_front<25, neither transition fires, leaving enter_hwy stuck if dist_to_front never reaches >=25. This partial gap is a source-level guard-completeness/disjointness concern reflected in the extracted obligation NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DISJOINT-1 and the transition group for NL-GROUP-NL3-1 showing both alternatives sharing the identical guard 'dist_to_front<25 and extra_lane=true' in the contract extraction (though the source text as authored differentiates the enter_hwy>=25 case using a distinct event). This is flagged as D1 because guard non-disjointness/gaps are implicit well-formedness concerns rather than an explicit NL rule, and one can argue the NL's informal conditions were never meant to be formally exhaustive/exclusive -- runtime environments may guarantee mutual exclusivity of high_way/urban_way or dist_to_front ranges by external convention, which the model is not obligated to encode defensively.

report.claim: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is a top-level region never entered
report.where: PlantUML lines 51-59 (CollisionAvoidanceSystem state and its transitions); source_id CollisionAvoidanceSystem, CollisionAvoidanceSystem.collision_avoidance_deactive, CollisionAvoidanceSystem.collision_avoidance_active; FCSTM state:CollisionAvoidanceSystem:line:73, state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:74, state:collision_avoidance_active:line:75; diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL and EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE
report.reason: The requirements describe the collision avoidance system as a concurrently-operating safety subsystem: 'The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met...' (NL12/NL13), implying it runs alongside the driving mode and must actually be reachable/active. In the authored PlantUML, CollisionAvoidanceSystem is declared as a second top-level state sibling to AutonomousMode, but the diagram only has a single root initial transition `[*] --> AutonomousMode`; there is no `[*] --> CollisionAvoidanceSystem` and no fork/concurrent-region construct joining it to the machine's execution. Both the deterministic inspection facts and the verify_facts confirm this: `STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL` is raised for CollisionAvoidanceSystem, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active (lines 73-75), and the two event consumers for its transitions (pedestrian/rear/front detection and the recovery condition) are flagged `EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE`, refuted by verify_facts. Because the region has no incoming transition from any reachable initial pseudostate and PlantUML/FCSTM here provide no orthogonal-region composition connecting it to the rest of the model, the entire collision-avoidance behavior described in the requirements can never execute. This is an author-model defect, not a translation artifact: the missing entry point is present (or absent) identically in the authored PlantUML source (`state CollisionAvoidanceSystem { [*] --> collision_avoidance_deactive ... }` with no root-level entry edge into it), and the source_trace confirms an exact identity mapping of this state/transition structure from source to model. A competent alternative reading is that the author intended CollisionAvoidanceSystem to be a concurrent orthogonal region implicitly running in parallel with AutonomousMode (common informally in state-machine sketches), which PlantUML would normally express via `--` region separators inside one composite state; the diagram does not use that syntax, so under strict UML semantics as literally modeled, the region is simply unreachable. This is a substantial defect since it silently drops an entire requirement area.

report.claim: lane_change_urban's exit-distance transition targets the wrong Finish state (crosses HighwayMode/UrbanMode boundary)
report.where: PlantUML line ~38, source transition tr_0017 (AutonomousMode.UrbanMode.lane_change_urban -> AutonomousMode.HighwayMode.FinishState on dist_to_exit<0.7); NL8 in natural-language requirements
report.reason: NL8 states: 'In the lane_change_urban substate, the system transitions to straight if the lane change is complete or to exit_urban if the distance to the urban exit is less than 0.7 kilometers (`dist_to_exit<0.7`).' The natural language names a distinct urban exit target ('exit_urban'), but the authored PlantUML instead routes this transition to `FinishState`, which is textually defined inside HighwayMode: `lane_change_urban --> FinishState : dist_to_exit<0.7` (tr_0017). The source inventory confirms tr_0017's target is `AutonomousMode.HighwayMode.FinishState`, i.e. a state whose parent is HighwayMode, being reached directly from a UrbanMode substate without going through the UrbanMode-to-HighwayMode mode-switch transition. This is corroborated by inspection facts noting 'I_TRANSITION_TO_SELF_VIA_PARENT' and general oddities around FinishState. Reusing a single shared FinishState across both modes could be a deliberate design simplification (both modes 'finish' the same way when auto_finished or exit conditions occur), which is a plausible alternative reading if the author intended one common terminal state for the whole AutonomousMode composite regardless of which submode reaches it. However, the requirement's use of a distinct name ('exit_urban') and the fact that FinishState is nested only inside HighwayMode (not shared at the AutonomousMode level) support reading this as a modeling mistake: an urban-specific exit is misrouted into the highway submachine's local finish state, which is structurally inconsistent (a transition from a UrbanMode child directly into a HighwayMode child, bypassing the modeled UrbanMode->HighwayMode switch transitions that carry route tokens 21/23). Because a competent alternative interpretation (intentional shared terminal state) remains defensible, this is rated D1 rather than D2.

report.claim: collision_avoidance_deactive and collision_avoidance_active are unreachable from the root entry path
report.where: PlantUML: top-level '[*] --> AutonomousMode' plus separate 'state CollisionAvoidanceSystem { ... }' block with no linking transition or orthogonal-region separator; translated model diagnostics at lines 74 and 75 (collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active)
report.reason: The requirements (item 12) state the collision avoidance system 'is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state,' implying CollisionAvoidanceSystem is a live, reachable region of the overall state machine that begins operating together with AutonomousMode. In the PlantUML source, CollisionAvoidanceSystem is declared as a separate top-level 'state CollisionAvoidanceSystem { ... }' block, but there is no orthogonal-region (concurrent, '--' separator) declaration tying it to the root machine, and no explicit '[*] --> CollisionAvoidanceSystem' transition exists at the top level (only '[*] --> AutonomousMode' is given). As a result, the deterministic inspection reports 'State ...CollisionAvoidanceSystem.collision_avoidance_deactive is unreachable from the root entry path' and the same for collision_avoidance_active (diagnostics W_UNREACHABLE_STATE, lines 74 and 75). The reachability_graph confirms the root only reaches AutonomousMode and its descendants, never CollisionAvoidanceSystem or its children. This is a genuine well-formedness/reachability defect: a state region that the requirements describe as always-initialized and functionally necessary (collision avoidance safety monitoring) is disconnected from the machine's initial configuration, meaning in the modeled semantics it can never become active, contradicting requirement 12's expectation that the system starts in and can enter collision_avoidance_active. This is a defect in the authored PlantUML itself (missing orthogonal-region composition or missing initial transition into CollisionAvoidanceSystem), not merely a translation artifact, since the PlantUML text has no mechanism connecting CollisionAvoidanceSystem to the reachable root scope.

report.claim: Duplicate/ambiguous guard on enter_hwy outgoing transitions to cruise and lane_change
report.expected: The requirement implies two alternative, mutually exclusive outcomes from enter_hwy: one condition leading to lane_change (dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true) and, implicitly, the complementary condition (e.g. NOT(dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true), or simply reaching a safe cruising distance) leading to cruise. The two outgoing transitions from enter_hwy should therefore carry distinct, non-overlapping guard conditions so that the choice between cruise and lane_change is deterministic.
report.observed: Both outgoing transitions from enter_hwy (enter_hwy->cruise and enter_hwy->lane_change) are authored in the PlantUML source with the exact same label/guard text "dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true" (lines 12 and 13 of the .puml, transitions tr_0006 and tr_0007 in the source inventory, and events dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true firing both transition:line:24 and transition:line:25 in the closed FCSTM). This makes the model nondeterministic: the same event/condition triggers two different target states from the same source state, with no guard distinguishing which one is taken. This produces a nondeterministic choice point in the authored source and in the closed FCSTM (same event dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true enables transition:line:24 and transition:line:25 simultaneously from the same state enter_hwy), which is a structural defect independent of the exact missing cruise-condition wording.

report.claim: enter_hwy has two outgoing transitions sharing the identical guard event, collapsing the required distance/lane-vs-lane-change split
report.expected: The two transitions from enter_hwy (to cruise and to lane_change) should be guarded by complementary/distinguishing conditions, e.g. cruise when the distance is not less than 25m or no extra lane, and lane_change specifically when dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true, so that the choice between them is determined by the stated conditions rather than being nondeterministic.
report.observed: Both authored PlantUML transitions (line 12: enter_hwy --> cruise, and line 13: enter_hwy --> lane_change) use the exact same guard text 'dist_to_front<25 & extra_lane=true', which is preserved unchanged into the closed FCSTM as two transitions from enter_hwy both firing on the same single event 'dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true' (transition:line:34 and transition:line:35). report.claim: InMotion state lacks a genuine hierarchical composite structure for its substates
report.expected: Per NL4, Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching should be substates nested inside InMotion, forming a composite/hierarchical state with InMotion as the parent, so that any transition into InMotion enters the substate region and transitions out of InMotion apply uniformly to all substates.
report.observed: In both the authored PlantUML and the derived FCSTM, InMotion, Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching are modeled as flat, sibling states at the same level (all children of the root state), connected via plain transitions (InMotion --> Accelerating, InMotion --> Cruising, InMotion --> Approaching) rather than true UML composite-state containment.
